自己紹介、WeChatの交換、火鍋やカラオケ。言葉の壁をこえて、中国で一生ものの: Introducing yourself, swapping WeChat contacts, hot pot and karaoke. Get past the language barrier and make friends for life in China.
語学交換で自己紹介: Introducing yourself at a language exchange
上海のデザイン会社で働く伊藤さんは、中国語をもっと話したくて語学交換アプリに登録: Daisuke Ito, who works at a design company in Shanghai, signed up for a language exchange app because he wants to speak more Chinese. On Saturday afternoon, he has arranged to meet Xiaoyu, a university student studying Japanese, for the first time at a cafe near Jing'an Temple. As he waits, a little nervous, he sees a girl waving at him.
上海の大学で日本語を学ぶ三年生、二十一歳。アニメ好きで明るく、人懐っこい: Third-year student studying Japanese at a university in Shanghai, 21. A cheerful anime fan who warms up to people quickly.
上海で働く日本人デザイナー、二十七歳。中国語歴一年、火鍋が大好き: Japanese designer working in Shanghai, 27. He has been learning Chinese for a year and loves hot pot.
語学交換の相手同士で、初対面。中国の若者は初対面でもすぐに打ち解け、敬語もほとん: Language exchange partners meeting for the first time. Young people in China open up quickly even on first meeting and hardly use polite forms at all. Even with differences in age or status, it's normal to use 「你」 and call each other by first names or nicknames. Being easygoing closes the distance faster than formal politeness does.
こんにちは！ 伊藤さんですよね？ 林晓雨です。: Hi! You must be Ito, right? I'm Lin Xiaoyu.
こんにちは！ 伊藤大輔です。大輔って呼んでください。: Hi, hi! I'm Daisuke Ito. Just call me Daisuke.
「你好你好」と重ねると、うれしさや歓迎の気持ちが出ます。日本の名前は中国語読みに: Repeating it as 「你好你好」 conveys happiness and a sense of welcome. Japanese names are read with Chinese pronunciations, so 「大辅」 becomes 「Dàfǔ」. Telling people up front what you'd like to be called puts them at ease too.
大輔、中国語上手だね！ どれくらい勉強してるの？: Daisuke, your Chinese is really good! How long have you been learning?
一年ちょっとかな。でもまだあまりうまく話せなくて。: A little over a year. But I still don't speak very well.
「学了一年多」の「多」は「〜ちょっと、〜あまり」。謙遜は一言で十分です。日本的に: The 「多」 in 「学了一年多」 means "a little over" or "more than." One modest remark is plenty. If you keep repeating "I'm bad at it," the other person will have to keep saying "No, you're not."
そんなことないよ、上手だよ！ どうして中国語を勉強してるの？: Not at all, it's great! Why are you learning Chinese?
中国映画が好きなのと……あと、火鍋が大好きなんです！: I like Chinese movies, and also... I really love hot pot!
あはは、じゃあ来る場所は正解だね。仕事は何してるの？: Haha, then you've come to the right place. What do you do for work?
中国では初対面で仕事や年齢、出身地を聞くのはごく普通のこと。プライベートに踏み込: In China, it's perfectly normal to ask about someone's job, age, and hometown when you first meet. It may feel like they're prying into your private life, but it's a sign of interest in you. After you answer, ask back with 「你呢？」.
日系企業でデザインの仕事をしてます。晓雨は？: I do design at a Japanese company. How about you?
大学生だよ。日本語専攻で、今三年生。: I'm a university student majoring in Japanese. I'm a junior this year.
じゃあ日本語きっとすごく上手でしょ！: Then your Japanese must be really good!
まだまだだよ。これからお互いに教え合おうよ！: I've still got a long way to go. We can learn from each other from now on!
いいね！ じゃあ……WeChat交換しない？: Sure! So... shall we add each other on WeChat?
中国では連絡先交換＝WeChat（微信）の交換。電話番号を聞くよりずっと気軽で、: In China, exchanging contact information means exchanging WeChat (「微信」). It's much more casual than asking for a phone number, and saying 「加个微信吧」 on first meeting is perfectly natural. Apps like LINE and WhatsApp are hardly used.
いいよ、私が読み取る？ それとも読み取ってくれる？: Sure. Should I scan you, or will you scan me?
WeChatの交換は、片方がQRコード（我的二维码）を出し、もう片方が読み取るの: The standard way to add someone on WeChat is for one person to show their QR code (「我的二维码」) and the other to scan it. 「我扫你」 means "I'll scan your code."
僕が読み取るね。……よし、友達申請送ったよ。: I'll scan you. ... There, I sent a friend request.
届いた！ 週末空いてたら、一緒に火鍋食べに行こうよ！: Got it! If you're free this weekend, let's go eat hot pot together!
「一言为定」は「約束だよ、決まり！」という楽しい言い方。中国の「下次一起吃饭吧」: 「一言为定」 is a fun way to say "It's a promise, it's settled!" In China, 「下次一起吃饭吧」 ("Let's get a meal sometime") is often just a polite remark, but once it gets specific, like 「周末」, it's a real invitation.
w:叫|（名前を）呼ぶ；〜という名前だ: to call (by name); to be called
「我叫〜」＝私は〜です。「叫我〜就行」＝〜と呼んでね: 「我叫...」 = My name is ... 「叫我...就行」 = Just call me ...
「学了多久了？」＝どれくらい勉強してる？ 期間を聞く口語: 「学了多久了？」 = How long have you been studying? A colloquial way to ask about a length of time.
「但是」より柔らかく、話し言葉でよく使う: Softer than 「但是」 and common in speech.
理由を聞く。「为什么学中文？」は語学交換の定番質問: Asks for a reason. 「为什么学中文？」 is a classic question in language exchanges.
「特别喜欢」＝大好き。「很」よりも気持ちが強い: 「特别喜欢」 = to really love. Stronger in feeling than 「很」.
「你是做什么工作的？」＝何の仕事をしてるの？ 初対面の定番: 「你是做什么工作的？」 = What do you do for work? A standard question on first meeting.
「大一」〜「大四」で学年を表す。院生は「研一」「研二」: Year levels are expressed as 「大一」 through 「大四」. Graduate students are 「研一」, 「研二」, and so on.
「互相学习」＝お互いに学び合う。語学交換のキーワード: 「互相学习」 = to learn from each other. A key word for language exchanges.
中国の連絡手段の基本。「加微信」＝WeChatで友達になる: The basic way of keeping in touch in China. 「加微信」 = to become friends on WeChat
「我扫你」＝あなたのコードを読み取る。決済でも使う: 「我扫你」 = I'll scan your code. Also used for payments.
WeChatで「发好友申请」＝友達申請を送る: On WeChat, 「发好友申请」 = to send a friend request
w:有空|暇がある: to be free; to have time
「你周末有空吗？」＝週末空いてる？ 誘いの前置き: 「你周末有空吗？」 = Are you free this weekend? A lead-in before an invitation.
約束が成立したときの明るい一言: A cheerful phrase for when you've agreed on plans.
w:差得远|まだまだ遠く及ばない: to still have a long way to go
「还差得远呢」は褒められたときの謙遜。言い過ぎないのがコツ: 「还差得远呢」 is a modest response to a compliment. The trick is not to overdo it.
自分の呼び方を相手に提案する言い方。中国人は日本人の名字が言いにくいことも多いの: A way to suggest what others should call you. Chinese speakers often find foreign surnames hard to say, so telling people your first name or nickname up front makes it easier for them to talk to you. It makes you feel much closer than being called "Mr. Ito" all the time.
小雨でいいよ、友達はみんなそう呼んでる。: Just call me Xiaoyu. That's what my friends call me.
（今まで）……くらい……している: have been ... for (a period of time)
どれくらいの期間続けているかを言う形。最後にも「了」をつけると「今も続いている」: The pattern for saying how long you have been doing something. Adding 「了」 at the end as well gives the nuance that it is still going on now. You'll always use this when introducing yourself to say how long you've studied Chinese or been in the country, so make one sentence about yourself in advance.
中国語を勉強して一年ちょっとになります。: I've been learning Chinese for a little over a year.
上海に来て三か月になります。: I've been in Shanghai for three months.
ここで働いてどれくらい？: How long have you been working here?
文末の「吧」は、提案や誘いをやわらかくする魔法の一文字。「加个微信」だけだと少し: The sentence-final 「吧」 is a magic word that softens suggestions and invitations. 「加个微信」 alone is a bit abrupt, but 「加个微信吧」 has a friendly "let's" feel. It also sounds like you're checking what the other person wants, so it's easy to use even with someone you've just met.
WeChat交換しようよ。: Let's add each other on WeChat.
一緒に火鍋食べに行こう！: Let's go eat hot pot together!
語学交換、友達の紹介、趣味のイベントなど、同世代と初めて会う場面。名前→呼び方→: Meeting people your own age for the first time, such as at a language exchange, through a friend's introduction, or at a hobby event. Following the flow of name, what to call you, job or school, then exchanging WeChat, you can quickly make friends with young people in China.
初対面だからと「您」や堅い言葉を使い続けると、壁を感じさせてしまいます。また、謙: If you keep using 「您」 and formal language just because it's your first meeting, you'll make the other person feel a wall between you. Also, repeating modest remarks over and over or getting defensive when asked about your job or age makes it hard for the other person to keep the conversation going.
中国の若者にとって、日本人の友達はちょっと特別でうれしい存在です。アニメやドラマ: For young people in China, a Japanese friend is something a little special and exciting. Many of them want to chat about anime, TV dramas, and travel, so if you ask questions back yourself, they'll feel "This person is fun to talk to!"
中国の人は、友達になるまでがとても速いです。初対面で年齢や仕事を聞き、その日にW: People in China become friends very quickly. They ask your age and job when you first meet, exchange WeChat that same day, and the next week you're eating hot pot together. It may surprise you, but it's an honest sign that they're interested in you. The important thing is to talk without being afraid of making mistakes. The other person will try hard to understand what you mean. Another good thing about friendship in China is that once you're friends, they will truly help you when you're in trouble. Return the favor in small ways too, such as helping with their Japanese homework. Exchanging kindness is what makes true friends.
中国で初めて会った人と連絡先を交換するとき、いちばん自然なのは？: When exchanging contact details with someone you've just met in China, what is most natural?
中国では連絡先＝WeChat。友達同士なら「加个微信吧」と気軽に言うのが普通です: In China, contact details means WeChat. Between friends, it's normal to casually say 「加个微信吧」.
「扫」は「QRコードを読み取る」。「我扫你」は私があなたのコードを読む、です。: 「扫」 means "to scan a QR code." 「我扫你」 means "I'll scan your code."
「我来上海三个月了」の意味として正しいのは？: Which is the correct meaning of 「我来上海三个月了」?
三か月後に上海に来る: I'm coming to Shanghai in three months.
上海に三回来た: I've been to Shanghai three times.
上海に来て三か月になる: It's been three months since I came to Shanghai.
三か月前に上海を離れた: I left Shanghai three months ago.
「了」を文末にも置くことで、その状態が今も続いていることを表します。: Putting 「了」 at the end of the sentence as well shows that the situation is still continuing now.
中国人の友達に「下次一起吃饭吧」と言われました。どう理解するのがいい？: A Chinese friend says 「下次一起吃饭吧」 to you. How should you take it?
必ず来週行く約束: A firm promise to go next week
社交辞令のこともあるので、本当に行きたければ日にちを提案する: It may just be a polite remark, so if you really want to go, suggest a date.
もう会いたくないという意味: It means they don't want to see you again.
日本と同じく社交辞令のこともあります。行きたいなら「周六怎么样？」と具体的に提案: As in many cultures, it may just be a polite remark. If you'd like to go, try suggesting something specific, like 「周六怎么样？」.
